intended_object: A dissociated exchangeable random graph law (Diaconis–Janson, Section 5): one where the induced subgraphs on any two disjoint vertex sets are independent. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the cited reference.
explanation:
An `ExchangeableGraphLaw` is a family of probability measures on `SimpleGraph (Fin k)`. The family is consistent under restriction along every injection `Fin k ↪ Fin l`, which also gives exchangeability.

The definition requires, for all `k` and `l`, that the joint law of the pair (restriction to the first `k` labels, restriction to the last `l` labels) under `law (k+l)` equals `law k ⊗ law l`. That is exactly independence of the two restrictions, with each marginal correct.

The literature quantifies over arbitrary disjoint finite vertex sets A and B. Restricting to the first `k` and last `l` labels loses nothing: by consistency along injections, any two disjoint windows can be relabelled as these two blocks, and labels outside them can be dropped. The module documentation makes the same argument.

Degenerate cases are fine. When `k = 0` or `l = 0`, one factor is a probability measure on a one-point space, so the identity holds trivially. On a finite vertex type the measurable structure on `SimpleGraph` is discrete, since singletons are measurable, so equality of measures is the right notion.

The setting, exchangeable random graphs on ℕ described through their finite marginals, is the standard one for this notion. Mathlib has no general notion of a dissociated graph law to compare against.
